input:
A gravity settler is employed in order to remove calcium carbonate from a process stream. The settler is sized on the basis of the overflow rate, which may be understood as the upward velocity of the clarified liquid at which a particle settling at that rate is only just carried over to the overflow. At a throughput of 218 m3 h-1 and with a design overflow rate of 0.72 m h-1, the required plan area works out to 303 m2: the area is simply the throughput divided by the overflow rate, and it is the area, rather than the depth, that fixes the separation, since a particle has the whole depth of the tank in which to settle, whereas it is only the plan area that sets the upward velocity which it must beat.

The overflow-rate basis relied upon here is a vendor rule for this particular solid. It should be noted that no settling test on the actual slurry has been carried out, and the area therefore stands on that limitation: a slurry whose particles are finer, or whose liquid is more viscous, than the vendor's reference material will settle more slowly, and at the same throughput the shortfall would manifest itself as solids carried over in the overflow. The vendor figure is, in essence, an estimate carried over from other slurries of the same solid, rather than a measurement performed on this one, and the settling test on the actual slurry represents the check that would replace it with a firm datum.
target:
A gravity settler removes calcium carbonate from a process stream. The settler is sized on the overflow rate, the upward velocity of the clarified liquid at which a particle settling at that rate is just carried to the overflow. At a throughput of 218 m3 h-1 and a design overflow rate of 0.72 m h-1, the required plan area is 303 m2: the area is the throughput divided by the overflow rate, and it is the area, not the depth, that fixes the separation, since a particle has the depth of the tank in which to settle but only the plan area sets the upward velocity it must beat. Depth buys residence time rather than capacity: doubling the depth at the same plan area leaves the overflow rate, and with it the fineness of the cut the settler makes, unchanged.

The overflow-rate basis is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, and the area stands on that limitation: a slurry whose particles are finer, or whose liquid is more viscous, than the vendor's reference material settles more slowly, and at the same throughput the shortfall would appear as solids carried over in the overflow. The vendor figure is an estimate carried from other slurries of the same solid, not a measurement on this one, and the settling test on the actual slurry is the check that would replace it with a datum.
